data.title: Database Migration
data.tagline: An ordered, versioned, and traceable set of steps for changing database structure or required data.
data.learningOutcome: You can require a compatible-add, backfill, verify, and constrain sequence, then accept it using migration history and data checks.
data.description: Suppose users already contains live rows and a required status column is needed. A safe migration adds a compatible column, backfills old rows, verifies that no NULL values remain, and only then enforces the constraint. The migration tool records applied versions, but migration files are not data backups and do not guarantee lossless reversal.

learning.assumes: You know databases store business data in tables and columns, and live databases hold real records.
learning.outcome: You can require a compatible-add, backfill, verify, and constrain sequence, then accept it using migration history and data checks.

distinctions.label: Database
distinctions.explanation: Database is the system that stores persistent data; Database Migration is the versioned script set used to safely evolve that database's structure over time.

distinctions.label: System Rollback
distinctions.explanation: A Database Migration records how the database evolves; a Rollback returns an application or system to an earlier version. Application rollback does not automatically restore schema or deleted data.

explanation.title: Existing rows may not satisfy a new required constraint
explanation.text: Old rows in users have no status value. Enforcing status NOT NULL immediately can fail while those rows remain empty. Even if the database supports a default during the change, the value must reflect a real business rule rather than a guess.

explanation.title: Stay compatible, backfill, then tighten
explanation.text: First add a nullable status column so old and new application versions can keep running. Next backfill valid values under an explicit rule and record the affected rows. Only after NULL count reaches zero should the migration enforce NOT NULL.

explanation.title: Verify data results and old/new application behavior
explanation.text: Check the migration version, log, affected-row count, and remaining NULL values; any NULL means enforcement must wait. In staging, also confirm existing users can be read, new users receive valid status values, and both application versions work during transition. Migration history is not a backup, so destructive changes still need a recovery plan.

data.boundary: Migration files contain change steps, not a copy of live data. Dropping or merging data can be irreversible, so destructive work still needs an independent backup and a tested recovery path. Rolling back application code does not automatically restore the database.

lessonPractice.title: You need to add a required column status (NOT NULL) to an existing user table with live data. What is the safest migration strategy?

options.label: Staged migration: add a nullable column first, backfill existing rows, and enforce NOT NULL after verifying zero NULLs
options.feedback: Correct. Keep old rows compatible, complete the data conversion, verify it, and only then enforce the constraint.

options.label: Drop the live user table and recreate it from scratch, asking existing users to sign up and re-enter data
options.feedback: Incorrect. Recreating the production table deletes existing records and is not a migration plan for adding one field.

options.label: Manually add the column via a database GUI in production without checking any migration files into git
options.feedback: Incorrect. A production-only manual edit cannot be reproduced in other environments or reviewed through the project's versioned workflow.

data.agentPrompt: The users table already has live rows and needs a required status column. First inspect the migration tool, current values, and old-app compatibility. Then add a nullable column, backfill valid values, verify NULL count is zero, and finally enforce NOT NULL. Run it in staging and report the version, affected rows, NULL check, and old/new app read-write results. Do not treat a down migration as a backup.
